coverage.main: Read all seventeen pages of arXiv 1902.10899v4 (31 May 2021): Sections I-VIII, Tables I-VI, Figures 1-6, references and Appendices A-E (proofs, training details for all models, rotation attack, defense Table A1, visualisations). The corpus lists only the arXiv record.
coverage.supplement: Appendices A-E are embedded in the arXiv PDF and read; none adds a transfer result.
coverage.excluded_results: Table I, Figure 3, Figure 5 and Table III are white-box attacks. Tables II, IV and A1 and Figure 4 evaluate the detection defense. The diagonal cells of Tables V-VI are white-box. The Section VII rotation attack is white-box.

result_groups.locator: Section III-A Eq. 6; Section VI-A; Tables V-VI (p. 9)
result_groups.population: ModelNet40 test point clouds (2,468 in the official split) attacked by PG or MPG at Chamfer D_C = 0.03 on PointNet, PointNet++ or DGCNN, retained as adversarial examples of the source, and evaluated on the other two networks
result_groups.outcome: target pre-attacking / post-attacking accuracy on the transferred set
result_groups.evidence: Eq. 6 defines the adversarial set B as examples the source classifies correctly and misclassifies after attack. The source diagonal cells read 100.0 / 0.00, whereas white-box PG at D_C = 0.03 leaves PointNet at 39.38% accuracy on the full test set (Table I). The arithmetic confirms that transfer is evaluated only on source-correct, source-successful examples. Target pre-attack accuracies below 100% (e.g., 94.63, 80.30) show the set is not restricted to target-clean-correct examples.

result_groups.population: MNIST point clouds attacked by PG on PointNet (source post-attack accuracy 21%), converted to images and fed to a LeNet-like CNN
result_groups.evidence: It is not stated whether the converted set contains all attacked inputs or only source-successful ones, or whether the 99.1% clean accuracy is measured on the same inputs.

result_groups.population: MNIST adversarial images from the CNN at several attack intensities, converted to point clouds and fed to PointNet
result_groups.outcome: PointNet accuracy (graphical; 98.9% in the worst case)

f1.locator: Tables V-VI pre-attacking accuracies; Section VI-B; Table I text (89.20%)
f1.evidence: Every PC-Net transfer cell prints the target's clean accuracy on the same transferred set, and the MNIST scopes print clean accuracies for the CNN (99.1%) and PointNet (99.2%).

f2.evidence: The PC-Net scope explicitly includes target-misclassified examples (no); the MNIST scopes are unresolved.

f3.locator: Eq. 6; Tables I, V-VI; Section VI-B
f3.evidence: The PC-Net scope is source-success conditioned (yes, by definition and arithmetic); the MNIST scopes are unresolved. Positive conditioning evidence.

f4.evidence: The size of each source's adversarial set is not stated, so the two- and three-decimal rates cannot be converted to counts.

f5.locator: Eqs. 4, 8; Tables V-VI captions; Section VI-B
f5.evidence: The PC-Net transfer budget is an explicit Chamfer pseudo-distance (D_C = 0.03), a non-L-infinity/L2 geometry that is not converted. The PointNet-to-CNN attack budget is not stated.

f6.evidence: The paper links no code; the models were trained with official PointNet/PointNet++/DGCNN code, but the attack and transfer evaluation are not released.

artifact_checks.result: Zero results; the paper links no repository.

bounds_checks.reason: Pre- and post-attack target accuracies are on the same transferred set, but that set is restricted to source-successful examples, so max(0, pre - post) is a bound for that conditioned population, not the unconditional misclassification probability. Not extracted as an unconditional bound; recorded for the manuscript as positive matched-baseline reporting.
Clean and attacked populations are not shown to match.

limitations: Non-blind evidence audit. The PC-Net field 3 'yes' rests on Eq. 6's definition of adversarial examples together with the 100.0/0.00 diagonal arithmetic, not on an explicit filtering sentence; an independent recoder may prefer unclear.
